owner: CC (code+proofs). The design ruling that reshaped it is already given (Akien, 2026-08-06); nothing further is owed from him.
supersedes: write-scan-for-single-writer (cast and withdrawn the same day — its premise was falsified within the hour by the ruling below; see `why`)
intention: A CONFORMANCE TOOTH OVER THE FOLDER, NOT A SCAN OVER THE CODE: `verify_lab()` reads intentions-congruency-lab/ and the sources it is compiled from, and reports every file that is not byte-identical to a live source, every source with no copy, and every non-`_`-prefixed file with no source at all — WITHOUT writing anything. It is the read-only half of the door that already exists, and it is what lets a reader ask 'is this view currently true?' and get an answer that running the copier would have destroyed.
why:
IT WAS CAST ON A FALSIFIED PREMISE AND THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT. This ticket first existed as `write-scan-for-single-writer`: a scan over a verb (open(...,'w'), write_text, shutil, subprocess) to enforce Law 6 single-writer on the lab directory, cast because intentions_model_compiler's filed edge (c) had read 'until the tester import-scans for a second writer' and the import-scan, once built, plainly could not serve it. Within the hour Akien ruled the premise away, 2026-08-06, in his own words: intentions_model_compiler's job is to COPY all the intentions into one place; 'when an intention is formalized into tickets, those intentions could all update that folder rather than launching the compiler for it'; the compiler 'is supposed to run each evening, assuming that we've sorted who that belongs to so that device can launch it'; and 'the lab is a viewing surface only'.

So SEVERAL WRITERS ARE LEGITIMATE and one-writer was never the invariant. The invariant is DERIVED, NEVER AUTHORED. That is a smaller claim and, crucially, a cheaper one to check: a write-scan needs a mesh over a verb whose target is usually a variable, which is dataflow, which Cairn is not building — and it would still only tell you who COULD write. Comparing the folder to its sources tells you what IS true, exactly, with no mesh at all. The whole three-candidate coarseness question the withdrawn ticket carried simply evaporates.

THE FAILURE THAT PRODUCED IT, RECORDED BECAUSE IT REPEATS: an instrument was designed for a research-flavoured version of the problem while the plain answer — compare the artifact to what it is compiled from — sat one step away unexamined.

THE LIVED SYMPTOM, WHICH SURVIVES THE RESHAPE UNCHANGED. Someone fixes a wrong line in intentions-congruency-lab/. It reads like every other intention file in the system, because it is byte-identical to one by construction. Their fix lives until the next regeneration and then vanishes with no notice, and the charter that would have told them the folder is compiled is the file they were editing. Today the only defence is that CC knows better — a discipline living in one agent's habit, which is exactly what Law 4 calls a debt. Note the sharpening: regeneration makes a hand-edit TRANSIENT, not impossible, and an evening run bounds its life to a day. Nothing announces one while it lives, and that silence is what this closes.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy — and an IOU pointed at the wrong instrument is a debt that reads as a plan)

Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — the door's proofs measure that the DOOR behaves correctly when run; nothing measures that the folder is conformant right now, and running the copier to find out overwrites the evidence)
Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces — a hand-edit is currently silent for its whole life, then silently gone)
Law 1 (the seed claim: carry this one folder to a bare machine and regrow the system — which is only as good as the folder being true)
watchme: none, because it rests at THINKME and the number worth watching is a rate the tooth itself will produce — how often verify_lab finds drift, which is the measurement that says whether hand-edits are a real event or a predicted one. Arming a watch before the tooth exists would be counting an occurrence nothing can yet detect. Answered when it is cast forward.
gates: proof gate beside intentions_model_compiler's code, under the tester. PAIRED TEETH: every catching tooth shaken over a planted lab (a hand-edited copy, a hand-added file, a source whose copy is missing — must catch) and over the real folder (must not). And the tooth must NOT run the copier first: a check that regenerates before verifying is vacuous by construction, which is this component's own version of the hollow green.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a drifted copy passes — the folder disagrees with its sources and verify_lab says clean; (2) a legitimate file is reported — the `_`-prefixed sources are authored on purpose and are not drift; (3) the check writes anything, which would make it the door rather than the mirror; (4) it reports clean over a folder or a source-set it did not actually read (import_sieve's HollowScan lesson, unchanged: a green over zero files is not a green); (5) it is only ever run BY the copier, which would mean it can never observe the state it exists to observe.
the_two_things_akien_named_that_this_doe: Recorded here so they are not mistaken for scheduled. (1) PER-INTENTION WRITE-THROUGH — 'those intentions could all update that folder rather than launching the compiler for it': sanctioned, unbuilt. Today every refresh is a whole-folder copy. This ticket makes such a writer CHECKABLE (its output either matches the source or it does not) but does not add one. (2) THE EVENING RUN — 'supposed to run each evening, assuming that we've sorted who that belongs to so that device can launch it': the ownership is explicitly unsorted and that is Akien's to settle. Worth putting in front of him when it comes up: compile-on-read already exists and fires (recompile_gate.sh, poked by /intent before it consults the folder), so the evening run's real job is the case a read never covers — a source that changed and that nobody has since consulted, and deletions. That is a smaller job than 'keep it fresh', and it may be that verify_lab reporting drift is the more useful evening act than a copy that silently erases it.
